title: closing-playbook-negotiation-journal
body:
Purpose: quick portable journal for last-mile redlines on mid-market SaaS deals. Not polished — intentionally terse. Use as call script + memory aid.

Context: late-stage negotiation with HealthTech prospect (PHI scope). They want: data residency EU, long retention for logs, broader indemnity, and agent access. We need to protect model IP, limit inference/derivative data exposure, and cap indemnity.

Priority clauses to watch (ordered by impact):
1) Data residency & processing: insist on limited-scope subprocessor list + customer-managed VPC for any private deployment. Do NOT agree to unrestricted export; propose: "data may be stored/processed in customer-designated region; where hosted, Redwood will use region X; cross-border processing permitted only for operational reasons with prior notice."
2) Indemnity: counter broad third-party claims for data use. Propose reciprocal indemnity for breach of confidentiality and IP only. Carve out claims arising from customer's unlawful data submission. Cap liability to committed fees (discuss exceptions for willful misconduct).
3) Security obligations & audit rights: customer requests unlimited audit window and right to image stacks. Offer sample SOC2 + 30-day notice and on-site remote audit limited to scope of Redwood-managed infra. For Private deployments, provide stronger access and support options instead of image access.
4) Confidential information & outputs: customer wants use restriction on outputs. Push back: outputs are ephemeral; allow customer use but disallow claim to Redwood model weights/derivative model training. Add explicit non-derivative clause.
5) Service levels & credits: they ask for hard p99 latency SLA. For hosted tier, propose operational SLO + credits tied to sustained breach (3 consecutive days) not token-level spikes.
6) Termination & data return/erase: ensure clear retention windows and export tooling. Avoid open-ended retrieval obligations after termination (use 60 days).

Negotiation signals and suggested responses:
- If they say "we need indemnity for data misuse by your models": respond with "We understand the concern. We can offer indemnity for breaches of Redwood's security obligations and willful misuse, but not for customer-submitted data content or downstream misuse by third parties."
- If they push for full audit rights: "We can accommodate scoped audits with notice and confidentiality protections; for our hosted service we cannot provide image-level access."
- If they insist on model training restrictions: "We will not use customer content to improve our base models unless explicitly contracted (opt-in). We can provide derivative-use guarantees and provide an opt-out mechanism."

Redlines to push hard on (language snippets):
- "Liability cap shall be limited to the total fees paid in the preceding 12 months, except for liability resulting from willful misconduct or gross negligence."
- "Provider shall not be liable for claims resulting from Customer's submitted data or Third-Party outputs generated from Customer prompts."
- "Provider may use aggregated, anonymized telemetry for product improvement; Provider will not use Customer Content to train foundation models without explicit written consent."

Redlines to accept with minimal resistance:
- Narrower service descriptions (ok to enumerate endpoints)
- Additional SOC report sharing under NDA
- Reasonable breach notification timelines (30-72 hours)

Walkaway thresholds (quick pick):
- Unlimited indemnity or uncapped liability requested
- Unlimited image-level audit access or ability to extract provider model artifacts
- Contract term that binds Redwood to indemnify downstream customer claims for outputs used outside of agreed scope

Fallback language templates (short):
- Data residency fallbacks: "If Customer designates a region not available, Provider will use the nearest available region and notify Customer within 10 business days. Provider will not transfer data outside the agreed jurisdiction for storage at rest without consent."
- Audit fallback: "Provider shall provide SOC2 Type II report and reasonably cooperate with auditor selection and scope. On-site or image-level requests shall be limited to Dedicated or Private deployments under separate SOW."

Phone scripts / call snippets (keeps it conversational):
- "I get the ask — security is top priority. For hosted, we can commit to SOC2, encryption at rest/in transit, and a mapped control matrix. If you need deeper inspection or image access, we can scope that under a Private deployment SOW."
- "About indemnity: we can cover breaches of our security obligations. We can also discuss a specific carve for regulated PHI processing, but unlimited indemnity for customer data content is a non-starter."

Open questions to resolve before final sign-off:
- Do we have an approved PHI addendum template for dedicated capacity? (PRIORITY: get from Compliance)
- Standard cap fallback: 12 months fees or 24 months? Legal leaning to 12; sales might want 24 for enterprise deals.
- Who signs off for exceptions on audit access? (SRE + Compliance + Legal)

Quick reference clauses (bookmarks):
- Data Use/Training: standard paragraph + opt-out checkbox
- IP Ownership: explicit provider ownership of model weights and algorithms; customer owns Customer Content and Outputs
- Escrow / transition: acceptable to propose limited code escrow for Private deployments only

Housekeeping notes (private):
- Keep email trail short and to-the-point; attach SOC and a short one-pager on deployment options.
- Loop in Solutions Eng when customer asks for performance guarantees — they need to sign off before promises.
- If sales wants to trade liability cap for higher price, document exchange clearly in SOW draft.

Action items (today):
- Pull PHI addendum draft from compliance (JIRA-REDEL-88) — Maya
- Draft liability cap language with 12-month fees + carveouts — Legal
- Prep two-level audit response (hosted vs private) + standard SOC link — Priya

Notes to self: keep tone collaborative; many customers lack infra nuance. Use "we can" framing not "we won't" until walkaway threshold reached.

Unresolved / scribbles:
- Customer asked for "model explainability" report for their prompts — what does that practically mean? Ticket a follow-up with Applied ML.
- Consider adding a short appendix of "common ask and one-line pushback" for AEs

End of journal entry.
